Darkened at ingest with gamma 1.6 rather than repainted: composition was right, only value was wrong, and the master keeps the bright original.

history.source: ChatGPT art project, 12 Sep 2026

chart/title.title: The Shattered Blue, from the title screen
chart/title.notes: The second chart painting. Darker and more evenly lit than chart/seas — sea luma 43 against 57, and a bottom edge at 43 rather than 73 — but it holds fewer separable chains (9 against 10 at a 20px dilation, 5 against 9 by area), and the chart needs ten. So it takes the title screen, where nothing has to be tapped and the dominant centre island is an asset rather than a crowding problem.

ships/blackfin.title: Blackfin
ships/blackfin.notes: Commission of 20 September 2026. Matches Part 4: black mainsails with a crimson lower edge over smaller cream canvas, dark oiled hardwood with no coral anywhere, an improbable density of small guns on swivels along an open firing deck, and the signature bright dotted line of brass muzzles running the length of the otherwise black hull. Crewed by Shoal-folk, correctly - small, large-eyed, big-eared - which settles the crew question the Swift raised. Guardrail holds: no troops, no heavy weapons, no coral mass, no scavenged clutter. One divergence recorded: the master calls for a medium narrow schooner and this is a twin-hulled craft, which reads as the same idea built the Shoal-folk way. Delivered 1448x1086, 4:3, no crop.

history.source: Sean, 19 September — production painting

ships/brig.title: Brigantine
ships/brig.source: Sean, 16 September — sliced from the fleet contact sheet
ships/brig.notes: Gun-brig (6), Free Confederacy. Replaces v1, which was a 234x174 slice off the original contact sheet and the last hull in the game still showing one - which is why she looked wrong beside twenty-seven commissions. A round-bellied twin-mast brig with mismatched patched canvas in cream, faded crimson and sun-bleached tan, a crowded working deck, cargo under an awning aft and a gun run out amidships with the smoke still on it. Dependable, adaptable and visibly lived in rather than sleek or derelict, which is her guardrail exactly. She flies the Confederacy's own skull-and-cutlasses, which is their sigil rather than a jolly roger.

history.source: Sean, 16 September — sliced from the fleet contact sheet

ships/bulwark.title: Bulwark
ships/bulwark.source: Sean, 16 September — sliced from the fleet contact sheet
ships/bulwark.notes: Replacement commission, 20 September 2026. Delivered 1448x1086, 4:3, no crop. Matches Part 4 point for point: long slab-sided armored hull on an extremely broad beam, low continuous weather deck, reduced ivory rig with dark green bands, overlapping black-iron bands over aged copper with brass gunport frames, and the signature four long-gun casemates projecting from the hull corners. Scene is the master's own - low across a narrow strait in clear daylight with lighter Crown ships working behind her. The no-castle guardrail is obeyed: the battlements in frame are the shore forts, not the ship.

history.source: Sean, 16 September — sliced from the fleet contact sheet

ships/chimera.title: Chimera
ships/chimera.notes: The Chimera: a retrofit with three colours of timber in her, a great crimson skull-and-cutlasses course, and a Confederate anchorage of stilt-huts and half-built hulls behind her. Well plated for her size and cheap to keep, which is the hull's whole argument.

ships/coral-class.title: Coral Class
ships/coral-class.notes: Living dreadnaught (102), Free Confederacy. Replaces v1. The brief's hardest half is the one it gets right: roughly two thirds of the mass is under water and legible through it, the battle profile above is a low armored back with the sea washing over it, and the recessed heavy-gun bays sit just clear of the waterline behind a colossal wedge reef-ram. Blood-red, burgundy and bone-white coral plate over the whole of it. No sails, no masts, and it reads as a warship rather than a submarine, a creature, an island or a palace, which is the guardrail. One divergence recorded: the stern carries a stepped, spired coral superstructure and a scatter of small upper turrets, where the sheet asks for no towers and an exceptionally low profile with only the ram and a small command ridge exposed. The silhouette is a broad wedge with visible underwater vanes rather than the single-centerline displacement hull the sheet describes.

history.source: Sean, 19 September — production painting

ships/cutlass.title: Cutlass
ships/cutlass.notes: Corvette (20), Free Confederacy. Replaces v2. Her signature reads: the pronounced rising bow curve the sheet asks for is the loudest line in the painting, echoing a cutlass guard without being a sword prow, and a heavy piece is run out over it threatening something larger - which is the class's whole argument. Compact full-bodied hull, crimson lateen canvas, a small white foresail. One divergence recorded: the sheet asks for LIGHT salvaged armor with brass edging and cream-and-crimson divided sails, and this is plated bow to stern in iron and reads considerably heavier than a compact corsair fighter - closer to a razee than to the Confederacy's conventional small warship.

history.source: Sean, 16 September — sliced from the fleet contact sheet
Sean, 19 September — production painting

ships/fenrunner.title: Fenrunner
ships/fenrunner.notes: Swamp raider (12), Crown Imperium. The brief delivered whole: long low flat-bottomed cypress hull with minimal freeboard, one short mast carrying a small warm-ivory lug sail edged in botanical green with a modest Crown emblem, a green Crown pennant at the masthead, poles and sweeps worked along both rails, light guns only, and reed and vine camouflage bundles lashed along the hull. Polished Admiralty brass on the lanterns and fittings is her signature detail and the one thing aboard that is not built to vanish. Preferred scene as written: poling a reed channel in misty morning light with half the crew watching the trees. Reads as a patient shallow-water raider, not a gunboat, a barge or a Marauder.

ships/ironback.title: Ironback
ships/ironback.notes: The Ironback: a captured Imperial two-decker cut down and plated over in bolted iron, a great bow chaser over the beakhead and a row of long barrels reaching well past her side, shelling a clifftop fortress through snow and storm light. The armour is patchwork over the old straight Imperial lines, which is the whole story of her.

ships/kestrel.title: Interceptor I
ships/kestrel.source: Sean, 16 September — sliced from the fleet contact sheet
ships/kestrel.notes: Commission of 20 September 2026, captioned 'swift 1'. Filed as Interceptor I, on the same reading that put 'swift 2' on the Interceptor II: the Swift is a Confederate Shoal-folk outrigger with no gun aboard, and this is a Crown cutter with a green pursuit pennant and a green-coated crew. Matches Part 4: knife-thin low hull, sharply raked bow, two raked masts and an outsized spread of fore-and-aft canvas, light timber with minimal bulwarks over a narrow copper strip at the waterline, ivory canvas with one green pennant and a small Crown emblem and pointedly no elite green sails, heeled hard in bright wind with a distant sail to run down. The guardrail holds - she is not bulked up and carries nothing heavier than a light gun. Slug is kestrel, the Interceptor I's art filename from before the v3 rename. Delivered 1448x1086, 4:3, no crop.

ships/kestrel-ii.title: Interceptor II
ships/kestrel-ii.source: Sean, 16 September — sliced from the fleet contact sheet
ships/kestrel-ii.notes: Commission of 20 September 2026, sent captioned 'swift 2'. Filed as Interceptor II on the evidence of the painting itself, which is that hull's Part 4 entry point for point and cannot be the Swift: the Swift is a Confederate Shoal-folk outrigger with no gun aboard, and this is a Crown warship under deep-green V2 canvas with a chase battery. The clincher is the master's signature detail for Interceptor II - 'five long chase-gun muzzles grouped into the sharp bow like a formal dueling pistol case' - which is exactly what is in the bow here, alongside the three sharply raked masts, the knife bow, the two Crown emblems and a distant fleeing target. The slug is kestrel-ii because the hull was renamed Interceptor II in the v3 roster and the art filenames never followed. Delivered 1448x1086, 4:3, no crop.

ships/majestic.title: Majestic
ships/majestic.notes: 1st rate (104), Crown Imperium. Replaces v2. Wins the way her guardrail says she should - through scale, proportion and discipline, and not through menace. Three tiers of gunports the length of an enormous gilded hull, a crowned lion figurehead, green-and-cream canvas carrying the Crown's crowned anchor-and-compass, and crew lining every yard and gallery in ranks. Nothing sinister, nothing coral-grown, nothing steampunk, and she reads as a ship that could float. The ARMOR CROWN of the fleet looks like the most expensive object in the world, which is what 2,610 gold and 1,045 days is meant to buy.

ships/sovereign.source: Sean, 16 September — sliced from the fleet contact sheet
ships/sovereign.notes: Commission of 20 September 2026, the first of the pair captioned 'sovereign 1 and 2'. Matches Part 4: gigantic three-decker, tall tiered stern, broad forecastle, three powerful masts, warm-ivory sail plan with deep-green panels and not an elite all-green rig, marines mustering on deck, a fortified harbor in warm light. Guardrail holds - taller stern and heavier, more administrative bearing than Majestic, not more elegant. Two divergences recorded: three Crown emblems on the sails where the master asks for one prominent emblem, and the ship's own rack of green-and-ivory landing boats along the quarters is not clearly read, the boats being in the water instead. ships/tempest.title: Tempest
ships/tempest.notes: Light frigate (26), Free Confederacy. Replaces v2. The scene is hers and nothing else in the fleet could stand in for it: carrying sail in weather that sends other ships looking for shelter, lightning behind and a torn sunset ahead, which is the one thing her entry insists on - a Tempest is rarely painted against a calm horizon because nobody remembers seeing one there. Black canvas edged in crimson, the Confederacy's own skull-and-cutlasses on the mainsail and at the masthead, an eagle-headed beak over a rising sea. Two divergences recorded: the sheet asks for a xebec-like medium hull, very long and low, with three raked masts carrying rust-crimson lateens mixed with small cream square topsails, and this is a conventional square-rigged ship of some freeboard in near-black canvas.

ships/urskin-goliath.title: Urskin Goliath
ships/urskin-goliath.notes: Leviathan conversion (64), Free Confederacy. Replaces v1. The structural half is exact, which is the half the guardrail cares about: the longest deep-bellied hull in the fleet in tar-dark timber, a continuous icebreaking keel carrying a colossal dire-whale skull and jaw at the bow, whalebone ribs braced along the side, a low heavy battery, and - her signature detail, drawn as written - two orderly banks of enormous sweep-oars coming out through iron-bound ports beneath load-bearing whalebone arches. Heavy crew on deck establish the scale, pushing through broken northern ice. Nothing sleek, coral-grown, cartoonish or monstrous, and every bone on her does a job. Three divergences recorded: four masts where the sheet asks for two modest ones, bone-and-slate checkered canvas where it asks for oxblood and smoke-black, and a kraken device on the mainsail where it asks for a Confederate flag beneath clan pennants. The light is a cold overcast rather than the rose-gold the scene note prefers.

ships/vanguard.title: Vanguard
ships/vanguard.source: Sean, 16 September — sliced from the fleet contact sheet
ships/vanguard.notes: Commission of 20 September 2026, captioned 'vanguard 1' and it is one. Matches Part 4: long low two-decker with a clean sheer line, modest stern, three evenly spaced masts, uncluttered gun deck, standardized oak with flush black-iron reinforcement over mature copper. Rig is the master's exactly - ivory sails with disciplined green accents and a single medium Crown emblem, against the II's green canvas and two. Signature detail present: the gold-painted measuring line running arrow-straight from bow to stern just below the rail. Pairs with the new Vanguard II, same hull and same headland, which is what that family's guardrail asks for. Two small divergences recorded, not corrected: the Crown emblem sits on the fore rather than centered on the mainsail, and she sails alone where the master's scene has her leading a small line of battle. Delivered 1448x1086, 4:3, no crop.

ships/vanguard-ii.title: Vanguard II
ships/vanguard-ii.source: Sean, 16 September — sliced from the fleet contact sheet
ships/vanguard-ii.notes: Commission of 20 September 2026, captioned 'vanguard 2' and it is one. Matches Part 4: the Vanguard's long low two-decker silhouette with a finer bow and a taller balanced rig, deep botanical-green sails with antique-gold edging, exactly two Crown emblems, bright maintained copper and brass-and-black-iron detailing, cutting through rougher water at speed. Signature detail present - the narrow gold chevron repeated at bow and stern that marks the second-generation frame. Not the Sovereign II, which is a four-masted three-decker whose own signature is nine recessed assault launches; neither is here. The family guardrail also checks out against the shipped Vanguard I: same three-masted two-decker and the same black-and-gold hull, with the upgrade carried by the rig. Delivered 1448x1086, 4:3, no crop.

ships/wayfinder.title: Wayfinder
ships/wayfinder.notes: Revision of the 20 September commission, same day: the earlier painting with a full bank of sweeps run out along both sides. Everything that matched Part 4 before still does - paired brass survey lanterns, chart-cabinet stern gallery, long covered waist, paired boat cranes, small battery, ivory sails with green edge bands and one Crown emblem, calm water off an uncharted island. The oars are an addition rather than a conflict: the master does not mention them and does not forbid them, and sweeps are exactly what a survey ship wants for working into a windless bay to take soundings, which is the job her entry describes. Recorded for the avoidance of doubt: oars are not galley slavery, and CANON v4.0 section 4 is explicit that the Crown keeps none - the oarsmen here are her own crew.

ships/witchlight.title: Witchlight
ships/witchlight.notes: Conjure sloop (10), Free Confederacy. Painting matches the v4 direction point for point: bound-jawed alligator skull at the bowsprit, bottle-charms and feathers and bead cords and grey moss in the rigging, cold violet on the deck guns and lanterns, and a stern altar of candles with one flower-crowned skull. The conjure sigil is dripping bone-white across a torn and patched mainsail, with a plain red Confederate pennant at the masthead and no skull-and-crossbones anywhere, which is her guardrail. One divergence from the sheet: the mainsail reads purple-black rather than faded crimson. The painting's palette is the stronger read and the crimson has moved to the pennant, so the painting stands and the sail line follows it.

ships/wraith.title: Wraith
ships/wraith.notes: Silent galley (12), Crown Imperium. Arrived captioned 'Fenrunner', was filed here on the evidence of the painting, and Sean confirmed it as the Wraith by re-sending the same image under that name - the file is pixel-identical to the first delivery, so nothing was re-imported. It answers the Wraith brief line by line: long narrow low black galley hull under sweeps, two raked masts with charcoal grey-green lateen sails, a bare knife bow with no figurehead, boarding grapnels and coiled lines tended along the rail, hooded crew, a small Crown pennant as the only marking, and the sheet's preferred scene exactly - closing on a lit ship across calm moonlit water with her own decks dark. One small divergence: the sheet asks for two banks of oars and the painting gives one, which suits a Small hull better.
